content.text: Cambridge International Examinations are the foundation of academic credibility for Eduversal Partner Schools. Examination integrity, security and fairness are a contractual requirement of our Cambridge Centre status. They also show our commitment to ethical assessment and international standards. This section gives a full working framework for managing all Cambridge assessments, from Checkpoint through IGCSE to AS and A Level. It helps schools comply with the Cambridge Handbook for Centres, protect candidate welfare and protect the validity of the qualifications issued. Key Objectives:

items: Run all Cambridge examinations securely, fairly and in line with the rules
Keep Cambridge Centre status by following the regulations and making the annual declarations
Protect candidate welfare and rights during the whole examination process
Give accurate, timely data to guide teaching, intervention and university counseling
Show assessment integrity to meet CIS/WASC accreditation standards
CIS Domain: Teaching & Assessing for Learning (Assessment Integrity)
WASC Category: B. Curriculum, Instruction, and Assessment; C. Support for Student Personal and Academic Growth
Cambridge: Centre Handbook compliance; Quality Management Standards
Indonesian Context: Links with rapor (report cards); data reporting to Dapodik (the national education database), where applicable

content.text: (See Section 3: Cambridge Centre Compliance for Centre registration and Quality Nominee responsibilities; Section 6: Assessment, Moderation, and Reporting for internal exam design; Section 8: Inclusion, EAL, and Learning Support for access arrangements.)
Clear roles create accountability and prevent gaps in examination management.
content.title: 10.2.1 Roles and Responsibilities

content.text: The Principal holds final accountability for Cambridge examinations. The Principal is also the named Head of Centre on Cambridge records. Key Responsibilities:
content.title: Principal

items: Sign and submit the Cambridge Centre Annual Declaration by the deadline (typically March)
Approve examination entries, timetable clashes, and special consideration requests
Make sure the school has enough secure storage, and monitor the key control logs
Authorize the appointment of the Exams Officer and the Quality Nominee
Oversee investigations of malpractice or maladministration and communicate with Cambridge
Review the post-results analysis and add its findings to the School Improvement Plan (SIP)
Set the budget for examination fees, invigilation costs and backup (contingency) arrangements
Report examination outcomes to the local Yayasan Board and add the data to EduNav dashboards
Signed Centre Annual Declaration (kept in a secure digital store)
Local Yayasan Board reports on examination outcomes and trends
Exam budget allocations and expenditure records

content.text:
The Exams Officer leads the day-to-day work on all examination logistics. The Exams Officer works closely with Cambridge and with internal teams. Key Responsibilities:

Before Examinations:
content.title: Exams Officer

items: Manage the examination entry process: check student eligibility, submit entries through Cambridge International Direct (CID) and confirm fee payments
Create and publish the internal examination timetable. Resolve timetable clashes using Cambridge-approved methods (rest breaks, separate sittings)
Coordinate access arrangements with the Learning Support Team (See Section 8.4)
Order and receive question papers and materials according to the Cambridge key dates for the series
Carry out secure storage audits and keep control logs for all materials
Train and brief invigilators using standardized checklists and scenario-based training

Prepare examination rooms. Make seating plans with a minimum of 1.25m spacing in all directions, measured from the center of one candidate's desk to the next. Put up display materials (clocks, notices, candidate information). Check the room conditions (lighting, ventilation)
Prepare the Cambridge Centre Annual Declaration for the Principal to review and sign. Make sure all compliance checks are complete
Supervise the opening of question paper packets following Cambridge instructions (check seals, count papers, record serial numbers)
Monitor invigilation quality through unannounced room visits
Manage examination incidents (fire alarms, medical emergencies, suspected malpractice) using the Incident Response Protocol (Template 10A)
Coordinate special consideration requests for illness, bereavement, or other adverse circumstances

Make sure scripts are dispatched securely to Cambridge on the day of each exam wherever possible. The Cambridge deadline is five working days after the exam (late scripts risk NO RESULT / X grade). Eduversal internal target: 48 hours. (Cambridge Handbook 2026, s.5.4)
Submit special consideration and access arrangements reports via CID
Collect and analyze the results data when it is released
Manage post-results services (enquiries about results, access to scripts, remarks)
Keep examination records for the period set in the combined retention schedule at 14.5. That schedule states the legal basis for each record type

content.text: Line of Accountability: Reports to the Principal. Works with Heads of Department, the IT Coordinator and the Facilities Manager. Evidence/Artifacts:

items: CID entry records and confirmation receipts
Secure storage audit logs (monthly checks)
Invigilator training attendance sheets and signed declarations
Incident reports and Cambridge correspondence
Post-results service requests and outcomes

content.text: Invigilators are the first line of defense for examination integrity. They must be properly trained, alert and fair. Selection Criteria:
content.title: Invigilators

items: Not related to candidates in the examination
Not teaching the subject being examined or year groups (where possible)
Passed safeguarding checks (See Section 9: Safeguarding)
Completed annual invigilation training and signed the Code of Conduct
Before the exam: Arrive 30 minutes early; collect materials, seating plans and attendance registers; check the room setup
Read the Examination Instructions to Candidates script word for word
Watch candidate behavior at all times; record any irregularities on the Invigilator Report Form (Template 10B)
Help candidates with permitted questions (timing, materials), but give no subject-specific help
Enforce the prohibited items policy (phones, smartwatches, unauthorized notes)
Keep the room silent and the session fair from start to end
After the exam: Complete attendance registers and incident reports; return all materials to the Exams Officer; keep all exam information confidential.
Cambridge examination regulations
How to identify malpractice (plagiarism, collusion, unauthorized materials)
Awareness of special consideration and access arrangements
Emergency procedures (fire, medical incident, bomb threat)
Resources: Invigilation Handbook (Template 10C), scenario-based e-learning module via EduNav
Signed Invigilator Declarations
Training logs and certificates
Completed Invigilator Report Forms

content.text: The Quality Nominee leads examination quality assurance and compliance in the school. This is usually a senior academic leader (Vice Principal, Director of Studies or an experienced HoD, Head of Department). Key Responsibilities:
content.title: Quality Nominee

items: Work with Cambridge on Centre inspections or audits
Lead internal quality assurance reviews (moderation, marking accuracy, procedures)
Make sure teaching staff hear about syllabus changes and assessment updates
Support the Principal and Exams Officer during malpractice investigations
Take part in Cambridge training webinars and share updates with the team

content.text: (See Section 3.3 for Quality Nominee appointment and annual review requirements.)
Each November, the local Yayasan Board receives an Annual Examinations Report. The Chief Academic Officer receives a copy. The report covers:
content.title: 10.2.2 Governance Oversight

items: Examination participation rates and outcomes (pass rates, grade distributions, trends)
Cambridge Centre compliance status and any notices received
Incident summary (malpractice cases, maladministration, appeals)
Budget compared with actual spending on examination fees and logistics
Recommendations for continuous improvement

content.text: Evidence/Artifact: Annual Examinations Report to the local Yayasan Board (Template 10D)

editorialNotes.title: Note (2026-08-20)
editorialNotes.text: Earlier editions of this section addressed the report to a school-level board of governors - a body that does not exist in the network governance chain (Section 1: Board of Trustees at network level; local Yayasan Board at school level). The recipient is the local Yayasan Board, with a copy to the Chief Academic Officer; the same correction was applied wherever this section referred to "the Board".

content.text: Cambridge examination materials must be stored in conditions that prevent unauthorized access, tampering, or environmental damage. Physical Security:
content.title: 10.3.1 Secure Storage Requirements

items.text: Dedicated secure room or cabinet with:
items: Steel construction or equivalent
Two locks (e.g., key + combination, or two separate keys held by different people)
Sealed access log mounted on the exterior
Environmental controls: temperature 15-25°C, humidity <70%, and a fire suppression system or fire extinguishers close by
Access restrictions: Only the Principal and the Exams Officer hold keys. Any access requires dual authorization and a log entry

items.text: Devices storing Cambridge assessment materials (e.g., on-screen exams) must have:
items: Encrypted storage and password protection
Network isolation during examinations (no internet access except where specified by Cambridge)
Antivirus and anti-tampering software updated before exam sessions
Visually inspect the storage area
Check that the locks work and the seals are unbroken
Review access logs for anomalies
Report findings to the Principal on the Secure Storage Audit Form (Template 10E)
Secure storage access logs (digital or physical ledger)
Monthly audit reports
Photos of secure storage setup (for Cambridge Centre inspections)

content.title: 10.3.2 Materials Handling

steps: Pack scripts securely in Cambridge-provided envelopes or approved containers
Complete dispatch documentation (manifest, special consideration forms if applicable)
Photograph sealed packages before handover (quality assurance)
Use a tracked courier service with signature confirmation
Keep proof of dispatch for the audit trail

items: Courier receipts and tracking numbers
Secure Storage Register entries
Dispatch photos and manifests

content.title: Script despatch deadline - the binding rule
content.text: Cambridge Handbook 2026: "If you do not send scripts back to us on the day of the exam, or within five working days after the exam, we consider them to be late. For late scripts, we cannot guarantee results will be released on time. We may not accept late scripts and we may issue a NO RESULT (X grade) on candidates certificates." Eduversal sets its own, tighter internal target so that the Cambridge deadline is never at risk. But five working days is the deadline that carries the consequence. Earlier editions of this manual gave 48 hours in this section and two weeks in Section 14; both were wrong.

content.text: Opening the Exam (15 minutes before start time):
content.title: 10.4.2 During the Examination

steps: Invigilators arrive and collect materials from the Exams Officer
Admit candidates to the exam room; check seating against the plan
Check candidate identity (school ID; photo check if the candidate is unfamiliar)
Confiscate prohibited items (phones, notes, smartwatches). Store them securely or ask candidates to leave them outside the room
Announce exam details using the Examination Instructions to Candidates script (duration, permitted materials, bathroom procedures)
Open question paper packets in front of candidates (verify seals, count papers)
Distribute question papers and answer booklets face down
Announce "You may begin" at the official start time; start the clock

items: Continuous vigilance: Invigilators walk quietly around the room and watch candidate behavior

Permitted assistance: Clarify timing. Allow bathroom visits one candidate at a time; an invigilator must go with the candidate to the door of the facility. Give replacement materials (pens, answer booklets)
Document irregularities: Any suspected malpractice (whispering, unauthorized materials, copying) must be noted on the Invigilator Report Form with timestamps and seating position
Do NOT accuse candidates during the exam; remain calm and neutral; investigate afterward
15 minutes remaining: "You have 15 minutes left."
5 minutes remaining: "You have 5 minutes left; check that you have written your name and candidate number on all answer sheets."
"Stop writing" command: At the end of the time, instruct candidates to put down their pens immediately

steps: Collect all materials (question papers, answer booklets, rough work) in a set order (row by row or desk by desk)
Count the scripts against the attendance register. Investigate any difference immediately
Let candidates leave one row at a time, so the exit does not get crowded
Invigilators complete the Attendance Register and the Invigilator Report Form
Return all materials to the Exams Officer within 30 minutes

items: Completed Attendance Registers
Invigilator Report Forms (even if "no irregularities")
Photos of room setup (for quality assurance)

content.text:
Sometimes a candidate is entered for two examinations at the same time. Cambridge allows these ways to solve the clash:

Option 1: Different Start Times (Supervised Rest Break)
content.title: 10.4.3 Managing Timetable Clashes

items: The candidate sits Exam A at the normal time
Supervised rest break (maximum 20 minutes) in a secure room. The candidate has no contact with other candidates and no access to phones or notes
The candidate sits Exam B immediately after the rest break
The Exams Officer must approve and document the arrangement
The candidate takes both exams at the same time in a separate room
Extended time may be required to complete both papers
An extra invigilator is required for the separate room
Complete the Timetable Clash Report (Template 10F) and keep it for audit
No advance permission from Cambridge is required when a clash is solved with an approved method

content.text:
Even with the best planning, incidents may happen. The Incident Response Protocol makes sure the response is quick and appropriate. Common Incidents:

Evidence/Artifacts:

content.title: Common examination incidents — immediate action and follow-up
rows: Evacuate calmly, following the fire drill procedure. Note the time and how long it lasts. Candidates may NOT communicate during the evacuation
If the interruption is less than 15 minutes, resume the exam. Otherwise, submit a special consideration request for all candidates
Allow the candidate to leave the exam, accompanied. Record the time. Offer a makeup if the candidate did not see the question paper
Submit special consideration for reduced performance or absence
Switch to the paper version if one is available. Note the time lost. Use backup devices
Report to Cambridge; request guidance on script submission
Note the seating position and the time. Do NOT confront the candidate. Allow the exam to continue
Confiscate the evidence (phone, notes) after the exam. Start a malpractice investigation (See Section 10.5)
Admit the candidate if they are less than 30 minutes late and have not had contact with others. Give no extra time
Record it on the Attendance Register. Consider special consideration if the lateness was caused by school transport or another valid reason

items: Incident Report Form (Template 10G) completed within 24 hours
Photos or confiscated materials (for malpractice cases)
Correspondence with Cambridge (for guidance or special consideration)
content.title: 10.4.4 Examination Incidents and Emergencies

content.text: Malpractice: Any act by a candidate that damages the integrity of the examination or gives an unfair advantage. Examples include:
content.title: 10.5.1 Definitions

items: Plagiarism: Submitting work copied from another source without saying where it came from
Collusion: Working together without permission on coursework or controlled assessments
Prohibited materials: Having phones, notes, or other unauthorized items during an exam
Disruptive behavior: Disturbing others on purpose, or refusing to follow instructions
Impersonation: Sitting an exam on behalf of another candidate

content.text: Maladministration: Any act by Centre staff (teachers, invigilators, administrators) that puts examination security or fairness at risk. Examples include:

items: Opening question papers early, or letting someone get to secure materials without authorization
Giving candidates unauthorized help during exams
Failing to report suspected malpractice
Poor supervision, or invigilation procedures not carried out
Making false attendance records or false special consideration claims
Not providing approved access arrangements. Or the opposite: giving a candidate access arrangements without formal Cambridge approval
The invigilator or staff member completes the Incident Report Form
Evidence collected (confiscated materials, witness statements, CCTV footage if available)
The report is sent to the Exams Officer and the Principal

The Head of Centre reports the suspected malpractice to Cambridge straight away. This report comes before any internal investigation and does not depend on one (Cambridge Handbook 2026 p.122, s.5.6.2; see 3.10). There is no grace period: no delay is allowed. Not reporting a suspicion is itself maladministration (10.5.1)
The Principal and Exams Officer review the evidence
If minor (e.g., a phone left in a bag by accident and not switched on): It is recorded as a warning. No further action
If serious (e.g., actively using a phone or notes, or copying): Move to a formal investigation
The candidate and parent/guardian are invited to a meeting (with 48 hours' notice)
The evidence is presented. The candidate is given a chance to respond
The meeting is recorded on Malpractice Investigation Notes (Template 10H)

content.text: Step 4: Internal Decision and Follow-Up to Cambridge (5-7 days)

items: The principal decides whether malpractice happened. The principal then sends the internal findings to Cambridge as follow-up evidence to the immediate Step 1 report. Use the Cambridge Admin Hub incident-report route and the current form named in the Cambridge Handbook
Cambridge reviews the case and decides the sanctions (warning, grade penalty, disqualification, ban from future exams)
School sanctions (if applicable): These follow the Student Conduct Policy (See Section 22)

content.text: Step 5: Communication and Record Keeping (7-10 days)

items: Tell the candidate and parent the outcome in writing
Keep all documents in the secure student record
Update the Malpractice Log (Template 10I). The log is used for the yearly report to the local Yayasan Board
Incident Reports and Investigation Notes
Candidate statements and supporting documents
Cambridge correspondence and sanction outcomes
Malpractice Log (confidential; stored securely for 6 years)

content.text: Access arrangements give support, arranged before the exam, to candidates with documented learning needs. They let candidates show what they know without an unfair advantage or disadvantage. (Section 8: Inclusion, EAL, and Learning Support gives the detailed procedures. The key points for exams are summarized here.) Common Access Arrangements:
content.title: 10.6.1 Access Arrangements

items: Extra time (up to 25%, or over 25% where strongly justified - see 8.6)
Separate invigilation in a smaller room
Reader or scribe support (for candidates with specific learning difficulties)
Modified question papers (enlarged text, Braille, colored overlays)
Rest breaks (for medical conditions that need breaks)
Word processor use (for candidates unable to handwrite)

steps: The Learning Support Team identifies which candidates are eligible. It uses diagnostic assessments or medical documents
Submit the application to Cambridge through CID (Cambridge International Direct) by the March deadline (May/June series)
Receive approval from Cambridge (or go ahead with Centre-approved arrangements, following Cambridge guidance)
Tell the Exams Officer, who arranges the room setup, invigilators, and materials

items: Diagnostic reports (educational psychologist, medical professional)
Cambridge access arrangements approval confirmations
Record of access arrangements used (stored in candidate file)

content.text: (See Section 8.4 for full Access Arrangements Policy and Template 8C: Access Arrangements Request Form.)

Special consideration gives grade adjustments after the exam. It is for candidates whose performance on the day of the exam was affected by temporary illness, injury, bereavement, or other adverse circumstances. Eligibility Criteria:
content.title: 10.6.2 Special Consideration

items: Candidate was present and completed the exam (or made a genuine attempt)
Adverse circumstances were beyond the candidate's control

Evidence (medical certificate, death certificate) is available. It is submitted no later than seven days after the LAST exam of the affected syllabus in that exam series (Cambridge Handbook 2026 p.117). The seven days do not count from the individual paper
Illness on exam day (fever, injury, severe headache) with medical certificate
Bereavement (death of immediate family member within 1 month of exam)
Accident or trauma (car accident on the way to the exam, witnessed violence)
Centre-related issues (fire alarm interruption >15 minutes, heating failure)
Long-term conditions already supported through access arrangements
Minor ailments (mild cold, exam stress)
Circumstances known in advance (family events, voluntary activities)

steps: Candidate or parent reports adverse circumstances to Exams Officer within 24 hours
Collect evidence (medical certificate, incident report)

The Exams Officer submits the special consideration request through CID. This is done no later than seven days after the LAST exam of the affected syllabus in that exam series (Cambridge Handbook 2026 p.117). The seven days do not count from the individual paper
Cambridge reviews the evidence. If it approves the request, it may make a small percentage adjustment to the candidate's mark. Cambridge decides the exact adjustment and does not disclose it.
Inform candidate of outcome when results are released

items: Medical certificates or supporting documents
CID special consideration submission receipts
Special Consideration Log (Template 10J)

content.text:
Cambridge releases results for the May/June series in early-to-mid August. Results for the October/November series, which is the main AS Level series, come in mid-January. The May Checkpoint series follows Cambridge's published release schedule. When results are released, the Exams Officer leads a full data analysis. This analysis supports teaching, intervention, and strategic planning. Results Analysis Protocol:

Step 1: Data Collection (Results Day)
content.title: 10.7.1 Results Analysis and Reporting

items: Download results from Cambridge International Direct (CID)
Upload them to EduNav, which builds the dashboards automatically
Distribute individual results to candidates (via secure portal or hard copy)

items.text: Heads of Department receive Subject Performance Reports (Template 10K) showing:
items: Grade distribution (A-E) compared with Cambridge global benchmarks
Component analysis (Paper 1 vs. Paper 2 vs. Coursework)
Comparison with predicted grades (from Mock exams)
Identification of topics/skills with low performance
Strengths to celebrate
Gaps that need changes to the curriculum or teaching
Student intervention needs for resits or next level

items.text: Senior Leadership Team reviews Whole-School Performance Dashboard (EduNav) covering:
items: Overall pass rates and average grades
Progress of subgroups (EAL, SEN, gender, socioeconomic status)
Year-on-year trends (3-year rolling data)
University entrance outcomes (% meeting offers)
Eduversal network average (benchmark across the 15 partner schools)
Cambridge global averages (published by Cambridge for each subject)
School targets (set in the School Improvement Plan)

content.text: Step 4: Integration into School Improvement Plan (Week 3)

items.text: Action planning meetings with Heads of Department:
items: Identify professional development needs (e.g., training on Paper 2 extended writing)
Plan curriculum adjustments (e.g., add more practice on specific topics)
Set targets for next cohort (e.g., increase A/A grades by 5%)
Update the SIP (School Improvement Plan) with priorities that come from exam results (See Section 4: Strategic Planning)
Subject Performance Reports (Template 10K)
EduNav dashboards (exported as PDFs for records)
SIP amendments and action plans
Professional development requests linked to results analysis

content.text:
Cambridge offers several post-results services for questions or concerns about grades. The Exams Officer manages these requests and consults candidates, parents, and subject teachers.

Service 1: Clerical Re-Check (Priority Service)
content.title: 10.7.2 Post-Results Services

items: Purpose: Check that all parts of the script were marked and added up correctly
Outcome: No change to marks (unless addition error found); very rare
Cost: Fee per the current Cambridge fee schedule issued to the Centre
Deadline: set by Cambridge for each series - see the key dates table in 10.3
Recommendation: Use only if candidate believes sections were not marked
Purpose: Re-mark by a senior examiner to check for marking errors
Outcome: Marks may go up, down, or stay the same (candidates must accept that the grade could go down)
Cost: Fee per the current Cambridge fee schedule issued to the Centre (refunded if the grade changes — confirm against the current fee schedule)
Deadline: set by Cambridge for each series - see the key dates table in 10.3
Recommendation: Use when the result is much lower than expected (e.g., predicted A, achieved D) and internal moderation suggests a marking error
Purpose: get a copy of the candidate's marked script for review
Outcome: Useful for understanding examiner feedback; does NOT change the grade
Cost: Fee per the current Cambridge fee schedule issued to the Centre
Recommendation: Use it for learning (to improve future performance), not for grade disputes

steps: Candidate or parent requests post-results service
The subject teacher reviews the candidate's performance data (internal exams, predicted grades, coursework)
The HoD (Head of Department) and the Exams Officer discuss how likely a grade change is
School policy: The school pays for clerical re-checks. Candidates/parents pay for reviews of marking (refunded if the grade improves)
Submit the request through CID by the deadline
Tell the candidate the outcome and update the records

items: Post-Results Service Request Forms (Template 10L)
Payment receipts and refund records
Outcome notifications from Cambridge

Cambridge sends examination certificates to the Centre about 3 months after results are released. This is November for the August results, and around April for the mid-January results of the October/November series
The Exams Officer checks that the certificates match the results data
Continuing students: Given out during assemblies or form time
Alumni: Collected in person (with an ID check) or sent by registered post
Cambridge charges a fee (approx. $50) for duplicate certificates
Candidates complete Lost Certificate Request Form (Template 10M)
Processing time: 6-8 weeks

content.text: Record Retention: Following Cambridge and accreditation requirements:

items: Results data and certificates: Kept permanently in a digital archive (EduNav + secure cloud storage)

Unused question papers and unused answer booklets/scripts: Securely destroyed (e.g., cross-shredded) after the post-results service window has closed. A destruction log must be kept. (This is typically 6 months after results.)
Access arrangements and special consideration documentation: 6 years
Malpractice records: 6 years (secure, confidential storage)
Certificate distribution logs (signature required)
Digital archive of results (backed up quarterly)
Destruction logs for question papers (with Principal authorization)

content.title: Appeals - the stage above an enquiry about results
items: An appeal follows an enquiry about results. A candidate must already have received an enquiry outcome before an appeal can be made.
Stage 1 appeal: made in writing. The Head of Centre must sign and support it.
Only the centre may appeal. Cambridge does not accept appeals directly from parents, guardians or candidates. Associate Centres appeal through their Cambridge Associate.
Stage 2 follows if the Stage 1 outcome is disputed.
Tell parents this at results time: the school submits any appeal on the candidate's behalf, and the school controls the deadline.
Source: Cambridge Handbook 2026, Section 7 (Appeals). Confirm deadlines against the current Handbook each series.

content.title: Access to Scripts
content.text: Access to Scripts is a separate Cambridge service, not a numbered enquiry service. The Handbook describes it as new and being launched in phases. It lets a centre download candidate exam scripts after results are released. Cambridge contacts the centre by email when the service becomes available to it. Earlier editions of this manual listed script return as "Service 3", which mixed it up with the enquiry services.

Sometimes a serious disruption happens (e.g., pandemic, political unrest, natural disaster). In that case, the Examinations Business Continuity Plan (Template 10N) keeps the harm to candidate welfare and qualification outcomes as small as possible. Key Elements:

content.title: 10.8.1 Examination Risk Register
content.text: The register below lists the main examination risks. For each risk, it shows how likely it is, its impact, and how the school reduces it.

content.title: Examination risk register — likelihood, impact, and mitigation
rows: Dual locks, access logs, monthly audits; insurance coverage for replacement costs
Fire suppression in secure room; backup secure location at sister campus; special consideration for all affected candidates
Backup devices (10% spare); paper version available; regular system testing
Keep a pool of invigilators 20% larger than the minimum required; keep an on-call backup list
Triple-check timetables (Exams Officer, Principal, HoD); publish 4 weeks in advance; candidate confirmation process
Thorough invigilation training; varied seating plans; review of scripts after the exam to look for patterns; zero-tolerance policy
Contact Cambridge support; use the contingency plan for university applications (predicted grades); inform parents early, without waiting for them to ask

steps: Communication Tree: Quickly notify candidates, parents, and Cambridge (within 2 hours)
Alternative Venues: Agreements made in advance with nearby Eduversal schools or public facilities
Remote Invigilation: Procedures for examinations taken at home (if Cambridge authorizes them)
Predicted Grades Submission: Strong internal assessment data to support Cambridge centre-assessed grades if exams are canceled
content.title: 10.8.2 Business Continuity for Examinations

content.text: (See Section 15: Risk Management, Emergency Preparedness, and Business Continuity for the full framework for keeping the whole school running in a crisis.)

editorialNotes.title: Note on this table
editorialNotes.text: This register scores risk qualitatively (Low/Medium/High/Very High on separate likelihood and impact axes) and never computes a numeric score, so it does not itself contradict the corpus risk banding of 10-14 High / 15-25 Critical. It is however inconsistent in method with the numeric 5x5 scoring used in Section 15, and it introduces a fourth impact level ("Very High") that the three-band scale does not carry. Reconcile the two methods at the next review so a single risk vocabulary applies across the manual. The subsection lacked a 10.8.1 heading; it was restored on 2026-08-20 as "10.8.1 Examination Risk Register", the risk-identification subsection this table belongs to.

content.text: Each year, the Exams Officer and Quality Nominee lead a Post-Series Review. It is held in September for the May/June series and in March for the Oct/Nov series. Review Components:
content.title: 10.9.1 Annual Review of Examination Procedures

steps: Data Review: Look at results trends, post-results service outcomes, and special consideration approvals
Stakeholder Feedback: Surveys of candidates, invigilators, and subject teachers (Template 10O)
Incident Analysis: Review all incident reports and malpractice cases (anonymized, for learning)
Compliance Audit: The school checks itself against Cambridge Centre Handbook requirements
Action Planning: Decide what to improve for the next series (training needs, procedure updates, use of resources)

items: Post-Series Review Report (Template 10P), sent to the Principal and the local Yayasan Board
Updated SOPs (standard operating procedures) for gaps found or for new Cambridge requirements
Professional Development Plan for Exams Officer and Invigilators
Budget recommendations for the next academic year
Post-Series Review Report
Stakeholder survey results and analysis
Updated SOPs with version control and change log
Training calendar for next academic year

content.text: Cambridge may carry out inspections, announced or unannounced, to check Centre compliance. The school stays ready for inspection all year round. Inspection Readiness Checklist:
content.title: 10.9.2 Cambridge Centre Inspections

items: [ ] All secure storage logs up to date (no gaps or unsigned entries)
[ ] Invigilator training records, complete with signatures
[ ] Access arrangements documents filed and linked to the right candidates
[ ] Examination room photos and seating plans archived
[ ] Malpractice investigations documented with Cambridge correspondence
[ ] Annual Declaration signed and submitted on time
[ ] Quality Nominee takes an active part in Cambridge webinars (certificates on file)

steps: Welcome the inspector and give them a workspace (a private office with access to files)
Quality Nominee leads response to inspector requests
Give evidence quickly and openly (digital files through a secure share; paper documents with a sign-out log)
Hold an exit interview to understand the early findings
Respond to any recommendations with an action plan within the required timeframe (typically 28 days)

items: Share inspection report with the local Yayasan Board and Senior Leadership Team
Add the recommendations to the School Improvement Plan
Monitor how the corrective actions are carried out, using the EduNav task tracker
Inspection reports and correspondence
Action plan responses and completion evidence
Yayasan Board minutes discussing inspection outcomes

content.text:
Clear communication at the right time reduces anxiety. It also makes sure candidates are well prepared for their examinations. Communication Timeline:

Communication Principles:

content.title: Communication timeline to candidates and parents
rows: Examination calendar, entry deadlines, access arrangements process, fees
Entry confirmation, timetable clash resolution, mock exam schedule
Final entry confirmation, special requirements (access arrangements), payment reminders
Examination regulations, permitted materials, malpractice consequences, stress management
Individual exam schedule with room numbers and start times
Last-minute room changes, reminders, support resources
Individual results, post-results services information, appeals process
Outcomes of enquiries, certificate collection dates

items: Bilingual: All critical communications are in English and Bahasa Indonesia (See Section 16: Parent, Student, and Community Engagement)
Accessible: Plain language, visual aids (infographics, timelines), and formatting that is easy for EAL (English as an Additional Language) readers
Multi-channel: Email, SMS, website, student portal, and print, to reach as many people as possible
Transparent: Honest about timelines, costs, and limitations (e.g., "Cambridge results cannot be appealed directly by parents")
content.title: 10.10.1 Communication to Candidates and Parents

items: Communication log (dates, recipients, content)
Parent information session attendance records and presentation slides
Sample communications in both languages
Candidate feedback surveys on the clarity of information
Receive examination entry lists by December to check that candidates are eligible
Attend examiner training (Cambridge-led webinars or recorded sessions) to understand mark schemes
Provide predicted grades for university applications (based on internal assessments and Mock results)
Support post-results analysis by reviewing component performance data
Monthly updates from Exams Officer on entry progress, timetable development, and risk issues
Approval required for significant decisions (late entries, withdrawal of candidates, malpractice sanctions)
Budget oversight for examination fees and contingency expenses
Termly updates on examination preparation (via Principal's report)
Annual Examinations Report (post-results) covering outcomes, compliance, and recommendations
SLT meeting minutes with examination agenda items
Yayasan Board reports and approval records
Teacher training attendance logs

content.text: Cambridge charges a fee for each subject for each candidate. Costs vary by qualification level and series. Typical Fee Ranges (2025-26 Academic Year):
content.title: 10.11.1 Examination Fee Structure

items: Cambridge Checkpoint (Year 6/8): $30-50 per subject
IGCSE: $100-150 per subject
AS Level: $120-180 per subject
A Level: $150-220 per subject
Late entry surcharge: +30% of the subject fee
Post-results services: $30-150 per component
Standard entries: Included in school tuition fees (parents do not pay separately)
Late entries: Parent responsibility (if the student or parent caused the delay)
Resits or extra subjects: Parent responsibility
Post-results services: Parent responsibility (refunded if grade changes)

content.text: The Exams Officer prepares an Annual Examination Budget (Template 10Q) each March for the following academic year, based on:
content.title: 10.11.2 Annual Examination Budget

items: Projected enrollment by qualification level
Subject choices from option blocks
Contingency for late entries (5% of total)
Invigilation costs (substitution coverage for exam-day staff)
Secure storage maintenance and upgrades
Training and professional development

steps: Exams Officer submits draft budget to Principal (March)
Principal reviews it and adds it to the whole-school budget (See Section 13: Operations, Finance, and Resources)
Local Yayasan Board approves the final budget (April board meeting)
Quarterly spending reviews to compare actual spending with projections

items: Annual Examination Budget with line-item breakdown
Quarterly budget vs. actual reports
Yayasan Board approval minutes

content.title: Unclaimed certificates
content.text: Cambridge Handbook 2026: "You must keep unclaimed certificates in a safe place for at least 12 months from the date we issue them." After that period they are returned to Cambridge. Record collection against the Certificate Distribution Log.
The templates below help schools manage examinations in a standard, efficient way. All templates have version control and are available in EduNav > Resources > Examinations Template Management:

content.title: Examination management templates register
rows: Annual Examinations Report to the local Yayasan Board
Record of any exam disruption or issue
Annual survey for candidates, staff, parents

items: Version control: Each template includes a version number, an effective date, and a change log
Annual review: Templates reviewed during Post-Series Review and updated as needed
Accessibility: Templates available in Microsoft Word and Google Docs formats; bilingual where appropriate

content.text: The Exams Officer must keep their knowledge of Cambridge regulations and best practices up to date. Mandatory Training:
content.title: 10.13.1 Exams Officer Training

items: Cambridge Exams Officer Course (online or in-person) within 6 months of appointment
Annual refresher webinars offered by Cambridge (minimum 2 per year)
Eduversal network training (cross-school sharing of best practices, held twice annually)
Data analysis training for results interpretation and dashboard use
Project management for running several examination series at the same time
Stakeholder communication for parent/candidate engagement
Training certificates and attendance records
Professional development log in EduNav
How the learning was applied, recorded in the Post-Series Review

content.text: All invigilators complete annual training before the examination series begins. Training Content (3-hour session):
content.title: 10.13.2 Invigilator Training Program

steps: Welcome and overview (15 min): Why the role matters; legal responsibilities
Cambridge regulations (45 min): Examination instructions, permitted materials, prohibited items, special arrangements
Scenario-based practice (60 min): Handling late arrivals, suspected malpractice, medical emergencies, and technology failures
Documentation requirements (30 min): Completing attendance registers, incident reports, and confidentiality
Q&A and assessment (30 min): Knowledge check quiz (80% pass required)

items: 2-hour update session covering regulation changes and lessons learned from previous series
Review of incident reports from the last series (anonymized case studies)
Training attendance sheets with signatures
Quiz results (filed in HR records)
Signed the Invigilator Code of Conduct declarations

content.text: Examination data is added to EduNav. This gives staff a real-time view of the data and helps them base decisions on it. Key Dashboards:
content.title: 10.14.1 EduNav Dashboard Integration

items: Entry progress tracker (entries submitted vs. pending)
Secure storage audit status (green/amber/red indicators)
Upcoming deadlines (auto-alerts 7 days before)
Budget vs. actual expenditure
Results overview (pass rates, average grades, trends)
Compliance status (Centre Annual Declaration, training completion rates)
Risk indicators (incident frequency, malpractice cases)
Subject performance data (component analysis, comparison with predictions)
Student intervention tracker (candidates requiring support for resits)
Access arrangements status (applications pending, approved)
Individual examination timetable
Results notification (when released by Cambridge)
Post-results services status tracker
Entries: Uploaded to EduNav from Cambridge International Direct (CID) API integration
Results: Imported from CID and distributed via secure portal
Performance analytics: Created automatically when results are imported; updated with Mock exam data to help predict outcomes

content.text: Examination management practices follow the whole-school Assessment Policy closely (See Section 6: Assessment, Moderation, and Reporting). Key Alignments:
content.title: 10.14.2 Assessment Policy Alignment
Alignment between examination practice and Assessment Policy
rows: Consistent criteria across internal and external exams
Mock results inform predicted grades and intervention
Subject leaders calibrate predictions using internal moderation protocols
Turnitin checks, signed declarations, consistent sanctions
SIP targets revised based on Cambridge results

content.text: The school uses the KPIs (key performance indicators) below to check how well it manages examinations. It reports them quarterly to the local Yayasan Board and updates them in EduNav. Reporting:

content.title: Examination management key performance indicators
rows: ≥95% at grade C / 4 or above (scale A*-G / 9-1)
≥95% at grade E or above (scale A-E)
≥95% at grade E or above (scale A*-E)

items: Quarterly KPI Dashboard (EduNav) reviewed by SLT
Annual KPI Summary included in the Annual Examinations Report to the local Yayasan Board
An action plan is made for any KPI that falls below the target

editorialNotes.title: Note on this table
editorialNotes.text: The "Average grade improvement" row names EduNav as the comparative-analysis system. Section 20.7 flags EduNav as possibly a legacy product; if so, this KPI measurement method points at the wrong system and needs re-pointing along with the EduNav references in 10.12 and 10.14.

editorialNotes.title: Note (2026-08-20)
editorialNotes.text: The pass-rate KPI was previously a single row spanning IGCSE, AS and A Level, with one 95% target stated at the A Level grade span (A*-E). A*-E is the A Level scale only; IGCSE grades run A*-G (or 9-1), so the single bracket conflated two scales. The KPI is now split per qualification, and the IGCSE floor (grade C / 4) matches the graduation floor in Section 2.16.

content.text: This section directly supports the following accreditation standards and regulatory requirements:

items: Teaching & Assessing for Learning: Assessment integrity, fairness, validity, and reliability
Operational Systems: Secure materials management, record keeping, risk mitigation
Student Wellbeing: Candidate support, stress management, access to special arrangements
content.title: CIS Standards:

items: B. Curriculum, Instruction, and Assessment: Valid and reliable assessment of student learning; alignment with curriculum
C. Support for Student Personal and Academic Growth: Access arrangements for diverse learners; examination stress support
D. Resource Management and Development: Adequate facilities, budget allocation, and staffing for examination administration
E. School Culture and Environment for Learning: Ethical culture, academic integrity, fairness
content.title: WASC Categories:

items: Full compliance with the Cambridge Handbook for Centres (latest edition)
Timely submission of the Centre Annual Declaration
Quality Nominee active engagement with Cambridge support
Secure storage meeting Cambridge specifications
Malpractice prevention and reporting protocols
content.title: Cambridge Centre Requirements:

items: Integration of Cambridge results into rapor (report cards) per Permendikbud requirements
Data reporting to Dapodik (where applicable for nationally-recognized curricula)
Compliance with student data protection norms
content.title: Indonesian Regulations:

content.text: Evidence for Accreditation Visits: All templates, dashboards, logs, and reports listed in this section are kept as accreditation evidence. They are organized in the Accreditation Evidence Repository (EduNav > Accreditation > Cambridge Examinations).
The Exams Officer, Quality Nominee, and Principal review this policy annually. They do this after the October/November examination series is complete. Review Process:

steps: Post-Series Review Report (Section 10.9.1) provides the data foundation
Stakeholder feedback from surveys and focus groups included
Cambridge updates (regulation changes, new guidance) included
Lessons learned from incident reports and malpractice cases analyzed
Draft revisions circulated to Senior Leadership Team for input
Final approval by Principal and the local Yayasan Board (January board meeting)
Updated policy published on EduNav and communicated to all staff

content.text: Good Cambridge examinations management is a clear sign of a high-performing international school. When Eduversal Partner Schools follow the procedures, standards, and safeguards in this section, they show:

items: Firm commitment to examination integrity and fairness
Respect for candidates' rights to accurate, valid assessment of their learning
Accountability to stakeholders (students, parents, universities, Cambridge, accreditors)
Continuous improvement driven by data, feedback, and reflection

content.text: The Principal, Exams Officer, Quality Nominee, and all examination staff are responsible for upholding these standards. Their professionalism, care, and dedication make sure that every Cambridge certificate issued shows real achievement and opens doors to future success.

content.title: Annual examinations calendar (May/June series)
rows: Subject option blocks confirmed; initial entry estimates
Subject teachers submit to Exams Officer
Entries submitted to Cambridge via CID, before Cambridge's final entries deadline (21 February for June 2026)
Access arrangements applications submitted before Cambridge's deadline (21 February for June 2026; 21 January where a candidate needs modified question papers)

Scripts are despatched exam by exam, on a rolling basis. Each paper is despatched on its own exam day (Cambridge deadline: five working days after that paper). There is no single end-of-series despatch date. (Cambridge Handbook 2026, s.5.4)
Post-results services window (enquiries about results). Cambridge sets the submission deadlines for each series; see the key dates table in 10.3

content.title: Glossary of examination terms
rows: Pre-exam adjustments for candidates with documented needs (e.g., extra time, scribe)
Online portal for Centre administration (entries, results, correspondence)
The school/organization registered with Cambridge to deliver examinations
A distinct part of an examination (e.g., Paper 1, Paper 2, Coursework)
The Principal (or designated senior leader) accountable to Cambridge for Centre operations
Trained staff member supervising candidates during examinations
The point in each timetabled exam session when every candidate must be in the exam or under Full Centre Supervision. Cambridge sets it for the centre's location. Not the exam start time
Candidate actions undermining examination integrity (cheating, plagiarism)
Centre staff actions compromising examination security or fairness
The school's lead for examination quality assurance
Grade adjustment after the exam for candidates affected by adverse circumstances on exam day
Question papers, mark schemes, and other confidential examination documents

All staff involved in examination management should get to know this section and consult it regularly throughout the academic year.

editorialNotes.title: Note on this table
editorialNotes.text: The "June 30 - All scripts dispatched to Cambridge" row is not a defensible calendar entry. Cambridge requires each script to be returned on the day of its exam or within five working days after it (Cambridge Handbook 2026); a single end-of-June sweep date would make every early-series script weeks late and expose candidates to a NO RESULT (X grade). Replace with a per-exam rolling deadline. Orphaned image with no marker; placed in the 10.18 appendices block. The calendar also previously fixed the post-results services window as a two-week span in late August; that row was replaced on 2026-08-20 because the manual carried three different window lengths (about 2, 3, and 4-6 weeks). The deadline is set by Cambridge per series, and the single home for it is now the 10.3 key dates table.
